rss.summary: Introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro Kimi K3.1 Pro landed on the Kimi API today - it's not yet open weights, but Moonshot promise "Full model weights will be released by Nov 4, 2026". They're also offering a "Highspeed" version that's 2-3x faster, at twice the price (except for input token cache hits, which are priced the same). The US dollar pricing is $2.00/million tokens for input and $10/million for output - the same as GPT-6.1 Sol and half the price of Claude Opus 5.5. Moonshot's own benchmarks show Kimi as approximately level with Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra - beating them on a few benchmarks, coming close on others. rss.title: Rapidly scaling online storage to serve over 1 billion ChatGPT users (Part II)
rss.summary: Learn how OpenAI scaled Habitat with reliable multi-tenancy, global caching, and Azure Cosmos DB to deliver 12× faster reads for ChatGPT.
rss.text_excerpt:
All OpenAI products require fast, reliable access to data, provided by our storage platform, Habitat. It has to respond in milliseconds to over 1 billion users across 40 geographic regions. Our infrastructure faced an extraordinary challenge: supporting explosive growth and new use cases while continuing to improve reliability, performance, and product developer velocity. Solving that challenge required rethinking how our online storage platform was designed and operated. We constantly evaluated tradeoffs, following the pattern of: first become reliable enough for mission-critical product traffic, then fast enough for global users, and, finally, to deftly operate at massive scale. This two-part series explains how we developed Habitat from a simple client library and database into a globally distributed storage platform serving over 500 petabytes of data. Part I focused on Habitat’s evolution from a Python client to a service. It also covered the techniques that allowed us to push a Python-based service far beyond what many would consider practical. In this post, Part II, we walk through how we scaled the underlying storage component: Azure Cosmos DB. Through a close working partnership with the Azure team, we arrived at a viable multi-tenancy approach of co-managed containers, with excellent read performance at massive, global scale. Request Response Changes (CDC) As companies scale, infra teams often evolve from running single-tenant systems to multi-tenant ones. Single-tenancy, where every product surface team maintains their own system, reduces blast radius and provides easy ownership boundaries and workload isolation. As teams and product surfaces grow, this becomes expensive to run. Single-tenancy makes every product team responsible for capacity planning and often results in significant over-provisioning. Conversely, multi-tenancy assigns control to a centralized database team, with better knowledge and experience for provisioning resources. But multi-tenancy creates its own problems, such as noisy-neighbor issues, where one tenant consumes an unusually large share of the resources to the detriment of the other tenants. In Habitat, we had to weigh all these tradeoffs to design a reliable, efficient, storage system at scale. rss.title: AI Is Getting Good at Math. Here’s Why.
rss.summary: AI models are solving more mathematical problems. A pattern is emerging in their successes that could help us predict which problems they’ll solve next.
rss.text_excerpt:
The question that interests me is whether we can predict what kinds of problems these models will solve. What makes a problem tractable for an LLM, and what do these solutions have in common? If AI solves problems differently from humans, identifying the difference should help us decide where to point it. The unit-distance disproof has the richest commentary, so let’s start there. Problem complexity Here is a simple mental model. To solve any given problem, you need a sequence of hints or insights with work between them. This maps surprisingly well to simple everyday problems and to complex ideas like General Relativity (see Bonus). The sequence looks something like this: Insight -> time / effort -> insight -> time/effort -> solution. An expert would need fewer hints than a beginner would, as they would have more background. In his commentary on unit-distance proof, WT Gowers uses a similar idea: the difficulty of the proof is the shortest sequence of hints that would let experts reconstruct it. He calls it Kolmogorov complexity modulo experts. For the unit-distance problem, his hint sequence had three parts: Look for a counterexample. Take the best known construction and generalize it. Try a sequence of number fields of increasing degree, but work with prime ideals of bounded norm. Gowers’ proposed formula for complexity is 2^k + t, where k is the length of the shortest hint sequence and t is the work required to develop it. It is the sort of formula that looks rigorous right up until you try to put a number into it, which is more or less the point. Complexity grows exponentially with the number of insights you need to solve a problem. Most problem solving is the work between these insights. You have a eureka moment, then spend months developing the hint until another conceptual jump becomes possible. For an expert, time spent is a useful proxy for this work, hence t. Hand someone the first unit-distance hint and they still have to do enough work to reach the generalized construction. Useful, but post hoc. You can’t look at the problem and predict it would need x number of hints. So, a problem’s age, the number of tries, and the prize attached to it are common proxies to ascribe difficulty. rss.title: Securing our frontier model training environment
rss.summary: OpenAI explains how we strengthened containment for frontier model training and evaluation, including offline environments and high-compute red-teaming.
rss.text_excerpt:
This post describes how we secure the environments that we use to train and evaluate frontier models. These research settings differ from those in which customers use our released models: models in development may not yet have completed safety and alignment training, and we deliberately test them under adversarial conditions to expose weaknesses. Before making models available for broader use, we conduct safety and alignment assessments and put production safeguards in place. In order to work with software, AI models need computing environments: digital workspaces where they can write and run code, search for information, and attempt different approaches to solving problems. These environments allow models to practice these skills, while also restricting what they can access or do—helping contain the consequences when models make mistakes or exhibit misaligned behavior. But as models become more capable, they become better at finding ways around those limits. A sophisticated model might exploit a software flaw or misconfiguration to escape a sandbox, exploit an internal service to reach the live internet, or find unauthorized ways to communicate with agents in other sandboxes. The Hugging Face incident in July, as well as other examples of model misalignment ⁠ (opens in a new window) that we’ve observed, demonstrates how models with sophisticated cyber capabilities can bypass containment during their training and evaluation. In response to those incidents, we’ve substantially hardened the security of our research environments. Working closely with cloud providers, we’ve added new controls throughout our infrastructure, reduced the attack surface that agents can exploit, and improved our methods for detecting misaligned behavior and attempts to cross security boundaries. These protections overlap, so that containment can hold even if an individual control fails—a strategy known as defense in depth . Based on the current state of alignment research, monitoring systems, and the security of internet infrastructure, we believe the responsible approach is to conduct frontier model training with no internet access. We’ve implemented this policy and will maintain it until advances in these safeguards justify broader internet access. --- 一个现代化的可视化规则引擎平台，用于编排复杂的 AI 工作流。在无限画布上设计、测试和部署 AI 流程——无需编写代码。结合 [flowgram.ai](https://flowgram.ai) 的能力与 Java 服务端，提供生产级工作流管理。 ## 功能特性 - **AI Agent 侧栏对话** — 对话式生成工作流：CreatePlan 分步规划、Canvas 自动创建节点/连线、HTTP/Query 查询工作流、实时预览 token 与计划进度；会话可重命名、可审查。 - **Agent 配置中心** — 模型参数（Host/Key/Temperature/Max Tokens）、默认执行引擎切换（内置 AgentScope / 火山方舟托管）、系统提示词与知识库、工具定义目录。 - **Agent 运行观测 API** — `/api/agent/metrics/*`：工具调用、会话运行、事件流、LLM 调用账本与上下文占用统计（`AgentObservabilityController`，供管理端/运维侧消费）。 - **可视化画布** — 无限缩放画布，支持拖拽节点。通过循环、分支和条件逻辑设计复杂的工作流。 - **AI 节点类型** — 内置 LLM 调用、代码执行、HTTP 请求、字符串格式化和变量管理节点。 - **实时预览** — 测试单个节点或整个工作流，实时查看输入输出和执行历史。 - **版本管理** — 每次保存创建一个版本。版本间差异对比（新增/删除/修改的节点与连线）、切换生效版本。 - **模板系统** — 创建可复用的工作流模板。一键从模板创建新工作流。 - **可扩展插件** — 小地图、自动布局、吸附线、节点面板等。 - **多分支节点** — 多分支 + 组合条件（and/or）与 else 兜底，支持复杂分支逻辑。 ## 截图 ### 工作台与工作流 | 页面 | 预览 | |------|------| | **首页** — 国际化产品介绍页 | ![首页](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/boommanpro/gaia-workflow-engine/main/docs/images/screenshot-home.png) | | **在线演示** — 可交互工作流画布（可拖拽、可新增节点、不可运行） | ![在线演示](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/boommanpro/gaia-workflow-engine/main/docs/images/screenshot-demo.png) | | **文档** — 快速开始、环境准备、部署方案 | ![文档](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/boommanpro/gaia-workflow-engine/main/docs/images/screenshot-docs.png) | | **编辑器** — 可视化工作流编辑器，含版本管理 | ![编辑器](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/boommanpro/gaia-workflow-engine/main/docs/images/screenshot-editor.png) | | **管理后台 · 工作流** — 工作流管理控制台 | ![管理工作流](https [TRUNCATED]

# NarraFork 简体中文 · [English](README_EN.md) **多人协作 多模型协作 多设备流转 的高效Durable Harness** NarraFork 是一个自托管的 AI 编程协作工作台。部署在自己的电脑或服务器上，你（和你的团队）在浏览器里组织 AI 会话、操作代码与终端、管理 Agent 的上下文和权限。 [快速开始](#快速开始) · [核心能力](#核心能力) · [参与开发](#参与开发) · [文档](#文档) · [许可证](#许可证) ![NarraFork 会话与文件预览](docs/images/overview.png) ## 核心能力 | 能力 | 可以做什么 | | --- | --- | | 多会话工作区 | [组织会话面板](#组织会话面板)，保存和恢复布局，在多个任务之间切换 | | 多 Agent 协作 | 委派探索、实现和评审任务，[直接向子 Agent 发送消息与接手讨论](#向子-agent-发送消息与接手讨论) | | 上下文管理 | [低成本分叉](#低成本分叉)、[可逆可编辑的压缩](#可逆可编辑的压缩)，为你带来前所未有的上下文掌控力 | | 开发工具 | 读取和编辑文件、搜索代码、运行命令，使用[交互式终端](#交互式终端)和 Git 工作流 | | 权限与审批 | 为目录和命令配置访问规则，对需要授权的操作进行审批 | | 模型接入 | 配置不同模型供应商，包括 Anthropic、OpenAI等接入协议 | | 扩展与自动化 | 使用技能Skills、例程和 MCP 工具，把重复工作组织成可复用流程 | | 团队知识 | 共享项目、站内消息和知识库，通过分级与标签控制知识访问 | | 跨设备工作 | 通过浏览器访问，[连接远程执行设备](#连接远程执行设备)，[在手机上跟进任务](#在手机上跟进任务) | 目前支持简体中文和英文，架构已为支持更多语言做准备，欢迎贡献你的翻译。 ## 特色详解 ### 低成本分叉 ![从历史消息处分叉](docs/images/fork-from-message.png) NarraFork 不为每个会话单独存储一份 JSONL，而是将消息存入数据库。分叉时只复制必要的引用，共享的上下文数据只占一份空间，不会随着分叉反复复制。 ### 可逆可编辑的压缩 每次压缩都会在对话中留下一个“压缩标记”。标记前的对话对人类依旧可见，但对模型来说已被替换成压缩结果。通过标记，你可以查看和编辑摘要，也可以撤回这次压缩，恢复对应的历史上下文。压缩不再是不可见、不可改的一次性操作。 ![对话中的压缩标记](docs/images/compact-marker.png) ![压缩摘要的撤回与编辑操作](docs/images/compact-actions.png) ### 交互式终端 不用每次执行命令都重复填写环境变量，或加上一长串 `ssh`、`sshpass` 前缀。在交互式终端里登录远程机器、设置好环境变量后，Agent 就能在同一会话中连续执行所需指令。你可以实时看到输入输出，并随时介入操作。 ### 组织会话面板 从左侧 RecentTabs 拖动会话到右侧，即可创建工作区，在同一个界面里同时管理多个会话。 ![工作区中并排管理多个会话](docs/images/workspace.png) ### 向子 Agent 发送消息与接手讨论 你可以直接点开子 Agent 的会话，向它发送消息、补充要求，或接手继续讨论，无需经过主 Agent 转达。 ![直接打开子 Agent 会话并交互](docs/images/subagent-conversation.png) ### 连接远程执行设备 ![在目标机器上安装远程执行器](docs/images/remote-executor-install.png) 连接你的电脑或服务器，让 Agent 直接在指定机器上读写文件、运行命令，无需来回切换工作台。 ### 在手机上跟进任务 ![手机上的消息左滑菜单](docs/images/mobile-swipe-menu.jpg) 手机不是临时凑合的入口，而是 NarraFork 的日常使用方式。我们为手机专门设计了交互，例如左滑会话消息即可打开操作菜单，让丰富的会话操作在小屏幕上依然触手可及，而不只是查看进度。 ## 快速开始 ### 直接运行预构建包 前往 [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/NarraFork/narrafork/releases)，在对应版本的 Assets 中下载适合操作系统和 CPU 架构的可执行文件，无需安装 Bun 或自行构建。项目与版本管理仍需安装 Git。 - **Windows**：下载 `.exe` 文件后直接运行。 - **Linux / macOS**：为下载的文件添加执行权限后运行，例如： ```sh chmod +x ./narrafork-<版本>-<平台>-<架构> ./narrafork-<版本>-<平台>-<架构> ``` 请将示例文件名替换为实际下载的文件名。 旧款 x64 芯片可选择带 `baseline` 后缀的兼容版本。注意：这并非以 AVX-512 支持与否为界；按 [Bun 当前说明](https://bun.com/docs/bundler/executables)，x64 构建已统一，`baseline` 保留为兼容别名。具体以该版本发布说明为准。 启动后打开 `http://localhost:7778`；实际地址以启动日志为准。 ### 从源码运行 下载本仓库源码，并在仓库根目录打开终端。 ####

QQ Agent Plus 是面向 Linux 服务器的 QQ 群聊 Agent。它连接外部 OneBot v11 协议端，每次触发使用 独立的 OpenAI Chat Completions 会话，不依赖 DSH、MCP、Electron 或 Windows 运行环境。 ## 特性 下列能力均来自实际群聊环境中的问题修复，每条对应的失败模式与处理方式记录在[改动清单](docs/CHANGES.md)。 - **对话行为**：单轮分条发言，先判断图片情绪再回应，表情包清单常驻系统提示（常用的 + 没用过的轮换，条数可调），结束前自检。 - **发送链路**：网络层发送重试，QQ 系统表情，消息 id 归一化，内联工具调用兜底解析。 - **贴纸系统**：自动收藏并优先使用 QQ 收藏表情，查找兜底，同步护栏。 - **玩法与提醒**：轻量小游戏直接玩（成语接龙 / 猜数字 / 20 个问题 / 真心话大冒险；掷骰子、抽签、随机点名用 `dice` 与群成员名单）；**状态机主持的多人游戏**（数字炸弹、谁是卧底、狼人杀——轮次/计票/判定由系统负责，身份与夜间行动只走私聊，模型不会说漏嘴；实验特性、默认关，狼人杀还需在控制台白名单里勾选）；「X 点提醒我 Y」会落成**持久化提醒**（重启不丢），支持每天/每周/5 字段 cron 与 IANA 时区，可设免打扰窗口和抖动，离线错过的多次触发只补最近一次，到点被唤醒后用它自己的口吻说出来。 - **MCP 只读资源**：`node src/mcp/resource-server.js` 向任意 MCP 客户端暴露全局人物记忆、群梗库、待触发提醒三类资源；出口统一脱敏，不含会话记录、配置与凭据，也没有写路径。 - **主动发言**：三条链路各自可关（会话安静时发起话题 / 无人回应时补一句 / 模型自安排唤醒），多活跃时段， 间隔护栏，跳过原因日志，重启后补齐漏收消息。 - **模型接入**：思考档位按渠道翻译、按供应商/按任务分设（设置 → 模型 API → 「高级：思考模式」），服务商审核拦截重试，兜底模型切换。 - **语音**（转写与回复）：语音/音频文件/视频音轨转成文字再交给聊天模型（与模型是否多模态无关）。 **默认走 API Key 的托管服务**（预置硅基流动的地址：粘一个 Key、从官网拉一次模型列表就能用； 也可一键换成 Groq / 火山 Seed-ASR / 阿里云百炼 / 讯飞 / 腾讯云 / 百度 / 自建，各家对新用户多有免费额度）； 也支持**零 Key 的本机 whisper.cpp**（离线、免费，控制台里点一下就能装、也能完整卸载 [TRUNCATED]

# Brightspace MCP Server [![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/brightspace-mcp-server.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/brightspace-mcp-server) [![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/brightspace-mcp-server.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/brightspace-mcp-server) [![CI](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/RohanMuppa/brightspace-mcp-server/ci.yml?branch=main)](https://github.com/RohanMuppa/brightspace-mcp-server/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/github/license/RohanMuppa/brightspace-mcp-server.svg)](LICENSE) [![Node >= 22](https://img.shields.io/node/v/brightspace-mcp-server.svg)](package.json) > **By [Rohan Muppa](https://github.com/rohanmuppa), ECE @ Purdue** Lets your AI see your Brightspace classes, so you can just ask: > "What's due this week?" · "Am I passing all my classes?" · "Summarize today's announcements" · "Turn my lecture slides into flashcards" Works with Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, ChatGPT Desktop, Windsurf, and any other app that supports [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) (the standard way to plug tools into an AI). It only **reads** your courses — it never submits, edits, or deletes anything.

## Get started in 3 steps 1. **Install [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/)** (version 22 or newer) if you don't have it. Download, run the installer, done. 2. **Open a terminal and run the setup:** ```bash npx -y brightspace-mcp-server@latest setup ``` It asks for your school's Brightspace address, your username and password, and how you confirm it's you when you sign in (a phone app, or another way like a text message). Your password goes into your computer's own password store (Keychain on Mac, Credential Manager on Windows), never into a file. Before signing you in, it connects itself to Claude Desktop, Cursor, Antigravity, Codex, or Claude Code if you have them. On August 4, 2026, the UK AI Security Institute (AISI) published a report that detailed some concerning behavior it observed from Claude Mythos 5 during its testing of the model’s cyber capabilities. In AISI’s evaluation, Mythos 5 was given a capture-the-flag (CTF) cybersecurity challenge, in which it was asked to retrieve a protected piece of data (the “flag”) from a simulated network. Internet access was deliberately enabled (this was standard for AISI’s cyber testing at the time, but is no longer). The cyber safeguards we deploy with general release models like Fable 5 were disabled. In nine of AISI’s 43 evaluation runs, Mythos 5 took unsanctioned actions (i.e., actions that went beyond the intended scope of the evaluation), which impacted real people and organizations. In this post, which is being published alongside an independent report from AISI, we investigate these behaviors from Claude Mythos 5 further, to understand what they reveal about the model’s alignment. Like AISI’s report, we concentrate on the transcript (the complete record of the model’s reasoning and actions) from a single evaluation run. In this run: To capture the flag, Claude Mythos 5 was tasked with breaking into a small network of computers that AISI had built for the test, designed to resemble a real organization’s systems. It attempted—unsuccessfully—a range of approaches that targeted these systems using the methods that the evaluation intended. However, it also quickly found evidence that one of these machines periodically contacted GitHub, which hosts code repositories.
